source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: NWT Student Financial Assistance (SFA)
entries.description: The Government of the Northwest Territories' grants and loans for NWT residents in part-time or full-time post-secondary education. It includes Grants for Students with Disabilities: up to $4,000 a year for tuition, books, travel and accommodation, and up to $20,000 a year for costs such as a tutor, interpreter or special equipment.
entries.cost_note: Government grant and loan program; the page lists no application fee.
entries.evidence: This program provides financial assistance to eligible Northwest Territories (NWT) residents to assist with post-secondary education-related expenses.
entries.notes: CNAF links twice to the old ece.gov.nt.ca income-security page (once as 'FORMS and APPLICATIONS'); it now redirects to this page. Applicants must be NWT residents studying in an approved program at a designated institution and must reapply each academic year. Address is the SFA office (1st Floor, Lahm Ridge Tower, Yellowknife).

entries.name: Speech Language Pathology (Northwest Territories Health and Social Services Authority)
entries.description: The NWT health authority's speech-language pathology service for children and adults with speech delay, language, communication, stuttering or swallowing difficulties. It is offered across the NWT (visiting therapists or travel to a larger centre for smaller communities), and people can refer themselves without a doctor's referral.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Our Speech Language Pathologists provide a full range of SLP services, including the identification, evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, and management of speech delay, language development and communication disorders.
entries.notes: CNAF lists the Yellowknife Health and Social Services Authority at yhssa.org (now 'Sorry, the website has been stopped') and says it provides speech-language assessment. NTHSSA's About page says it was formed by amalgamating six regional authorities, including Yellowknife; this is its speech-language service. Yellowknife rehabilitation services have moved to 550 Byrne Rd; self-referral forms go to the email given.

entries.name: Services for Persons with Disabilities (NWT Health and Social Services)
entries.description: A Government of the Northwest Territories page that points people with disabilities and their families to territorial programs across departments, such as income security, home and community care, supported living, the Office of the Public Guardian, housing mobility modifications, the Public Trustee and property tax relief. It also lists partner organizations, including the NWT Disabilities Council and Inclusion NWT.
entries.cost_note: Government information page; it does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Each individual accesses different programs based on their wants and needs. Sometimes, the largest barrier is knowing where to start.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the Northwest Territories has fewer than 5 kept entries. Phone is Seniors and Continuing Care Services, Department of Health and Social Services; the page also gives the NWT Disabilities Council's toll-free line, 1-800-491-8885. No NWT autism society was found (autismnwt.ca, .com and .org do not resolve, and none is among this page's partner organizations).

entries.name: Income Assistance Program (Government of the Northwest Territories)
entries.description: A Northwest Territories Department of Education, Culture and Employment program that gives monthly financial assistance to NWT residents whose needs are greater than their income, to help meet basic needs. People apply each month at a local ECE Service Centre, where a Client Navigator can help with the application.
entries.evidence: This program provides financial assistance to Northwest Territories (NWT) residents to help meet their basic needs.
entries.notes: Not a Yukon resource: CNAF's Yukon page links an AIDE Canada guide to NWT adult funding and names 'Income Assistance' in unlinked text. The NWT also has a separate Income Assistance for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities program (listed in this page's menu). Toll free (866) 973-7252.

entries.name: Learning Supports for Persons with Disabilities (NWT Disabilities Council)
entries.description: A fund run by the NWT Disabilities Council that helps NWT residents with disabilities reach their learning goals. Adults 18 and older who are out of high school and cannot get training funding elsewhere, and organizations, can apply with a proposal showing how the money will help overcome barriers to learning.
entries.cost_note: Funding for learning supports, given by proposal.
entries.evidence: The Learning Support for Persons with Disabilities Fund helps NWT residents with disabilities achieve their learning goals.
entries.notes: Not a Yukon resource: named in unlinked text on CNAF's Yukon page (taken from an AIDE Canada guide to NWT adult funding). Contact details from the same page (Information, Referral, and Support Coordinator); toll free 1.800.491.8885.

entries.name: Information, Referral and Support (NWT Disabilities Council)
entries.description: A free NWT Disabilities Council program for residents anywhere in the Northwest Territories, with any type of disability; people can refer themselves and do not need a formal diagnosis. Staff give information about disability services in the NWT, link people to them, help with applications such as CPP Disability, Income Support and Learning Supports for Persons with Disabilities, and can go to meetings or appeals as an advocate.
entries.cost_note: A toll-free number lets all territorial residents use the program free of charge.
entries.evidence: This program is available to all Territorial residents regardless of where they live, or the type of disability.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. The Council's Learning Supports fund is already listed (cnaf_nt.json, nwtdc-learning-supports); this is its separate information and navigation program. Toll free 1.800.491.8885; the office is on the lower level of the Scotia Center in Yellowknife (the Contact page gives admin@nwtdc.net for general inquiries).

entries.name: Community Respite (NWT Disabilities Council)
entries.description: A respite program, funded by the GNWT Department of Health and Social Services, for families outside Yellowknife who care at home for children and youth with disabilities. The Council recruits and trains local respite workers (or a friend or relative the family suggests) to give planned relief at home or in the community; it runs in Deline, Fort Smith, Aklavik, Fort Liard, Fort McPherson, Inuvik, Behchoko, Whati and Dettah.
entries.cost_note: Funded by the GNWT Department of Health and Social Services; the page does not mention a fee for families.
entries.evidence: The program hires and trains local community members as Respite Workers to provide planned in-home or in-community relief for primary care-givers, families, and the children and youth with disabilities that they care for.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. Families can refer themselves or be referred by a health centre, social worker, school or therapist; the person cared for must live with family or a legal guardian and have a disability that needs ongoing (not specialized medical) support. The page also has an adult referral form. Contact is the Community Respite Coordinator; toll free 1.800.491.8885.

entries.name: Early Childhood Intervention Program (NWT Disabilities Council)
entries.description: Early intervention for children from birth to school entry who have disabilities or developmental delays. Early Childhood Intervention Workers give one-to-one support, usually in the preschool the parents choose (sometimes at home or a day home), working with parents and other professionals; the Council also has a Snoezelen multisensory room that families can book.
entries.cost_note: Funded by the GNWT Healthy Children Initiative, YHSSA, Jordan's Principle and others; the page does not mention a fee.
entries.evidence: The Early Childhood Intervention Program (ECIP) provides early intervention services for children between birth and school entry who have disabilities and/or developments delays.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. Parents, a physician or others can refer a child, but only with the parent's or guardian's permission (referral form on the page). The page does not say which communities are served; the office is in Yellowknife, toll free 1.800.491.8885. The email is the Child Services Manager's role address.

entries.name: Inclusion NWT
entries.description: A Yellowknife non-profit charity, part of Inclusion Canada, that has supported people with intellectual disabilities and their families in the Northwest Territories since 1962. Its services are supported living for adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities or brain injury who live in their own homes, respite for caregiving families, skills training and supported employment for adults with more complex needs, and employment services for adults with disabilities.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We provide lifelong support for individuals with intellectual disabilities and their families in the Northwest Territories, since 1962.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services; the GNWT's Services for Persons with Disabilities page (already listed) names it as a partner. People ask for support through the site's Apply for Support form. The email link on the site points to a placeholder address, so use the address as shown; mailing address PO Box 981, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2N7.

entries.name: Income Assistance for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities (Government of the Northwest Territories)
entries.description: An annual Department of Education, Culture and Employment program that helps NWT residents aged 19 to 59 with a permanent or long-term disability, and seniors 60 and over, meet their basic needs when their need is greater than their income. Funding depends on family income and community and covers actual shelter and utility costs; people apply at a local ECE Service Centre, where a Client Navigator can help.
entries.evidence: This program provides financial assistance to Northwest Territories (NWT) seniors and persons with disabilities to help meet their basic needs.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. This is separate from the general Income Assistance Program already listed (cnaf_nt.json, nwt-income-assistance). Applications are accepted from July 1 each year; phone is Income Security Programs in Yellowknife, toll free (866) 973-7252, and the page lists regional ECE Service Centre numbers.

entries.name: Office of the Public Guardian (NWT Health and Social Services)
entries.description: The NWT office for guardianship of adults 18 and older who cannot make their own personal or health care decisions. Anyone can call to ask about guardianship or request a referral package; staff explain how it works, look first at less restrictive options, start the guardianship process when it is needed, and can help prepare later guardianship reviews.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Anyone can call the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) to ask questions about guardianship or request a guardianship referral package.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. Guardians do not make financial decisions; trusteeship goes through the Public Trustee Office (867-767-9252 ext. 82447). The office is on the 7th floor of Centre Square Towers, Yellowknife. The URL /en/services/office-public-guardian redirects to this page.

entries.name: Supported Living (NWT Health and Social Services)
entries.description: A GNWT program for adults 19 and older with a permanent or long-duration cognitive, physical or mental health disability who need help with daily tasks to live as independently as possible. Based on assessed need, it gives non-medical support, from minimal help to 24 hours a day, in the person's own or family home or in supported living accommodations, with case management and respite for families who are the main supporters.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Supported Living helps adults with disabilities live as independently and safely as possible and participate fully in their community.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. The application is completed by a social worker, occupational therapist, nurse or adult service worker; day programs and skills training are not included. Phone is Seniors and Continuing Care Services, Department of Health and Social Services (the same contact as the Services for Persons with Disabilities page already listed).

entries.name: Special Olympics NWT
entries.description: Special Olympics NWT, based in Yellowknife, offers free sport programs for people with an intellectual or developmental disability. Youth programs (Active Start for ages 2 to 6 and FUNdamentals for 7 to 11) run on Saturday mornings from October to May with a parent taking part, and athletes 12 and over can train and compete in sports such as swimming, bowling, skating, snowshoeing, track and field and golf.
entries.cost_note: Taking part is free; athletes pay for their own sport equipment and families provide transport.
entries.evidence: Special Olympics NWT offers sports opportunity to individuals with an intellectual disability.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because the NWT has only 5 checked services. 2026-27 registration is open (online athlete and parent/guardian forms). The office is by appointment only; phone and email are the Sport Program Coordinator's (Executive Director 867-446-2266). The site is a section of specialolympics.ca.
